chapter_text:
CHAPTER 19 - PERIMETERS AND AREAS OF PLANE FIGURES

Introduction

Every plane (flat) closed figure has two basic measurements: the PERIMETER, which is the total length of its boundary, and the AREA, which is the amount of surface it encloses. Perimeter is a length, so it is measured in units such as cm, m or km. Area is measured in SQUARE units such as cm^2, m^2 or km^2. In this chapter we recall and extend the formulas for the perimeter and area of the common plane figures - rectangle, square, parallelogram, triangle, rhombus, trapezium and circle - and learn to handle arcs, sectors, segments and composite (combined) figures made by joining or removing simple shapes.

19.1 RECTANGLE AND SQUARE

A RECTANGLE has length l and breadth (width) b. Its opposite sides are equal and all four angles are right angles.
   Perimeter of a rectangle = 2(l + b)
   Area of a rectangle = l x b
   Diagonal of a rectangle = sqrt(l^2 + b^2)
A SQUARE is a rectangle in which all four sides are equal; let the side be a.
   Perimeter of a square = 4a
   Area of a square = a^2
   Diagonal of a square = a x sqrt(2), so area can also be written as (1/2) x d^2 where d is the diagonal.

Worked example: A rectangular field is 40 m long and 25 m wide. Perimeter = 2(40 + 25) = 2 x 65 = 130 m. Area = 40 x 25 = 1000 m^2. If a square has side 12 cm, its perimeter is 4 x 12 = 48 cm and its area is 12^2 = 144 cm^2.

19.2 PARALLELOGRAM

A PARALLELOGRAM has two pairs of parallel sides. If the base is b and the corresponding height (the perpendicular distance between the base and the opposite side) is h, then
   Area of a parallelogram = base x height = b x h
Note that the height must be measured PERPENDICULAR to the base, not along the slanting side. The perimeter of a parallelogram with sides a and b is 2(a + b).

Worked example: A parallelogram has base 8 cm and height 5 cm. Area = 8 x 5 = 40 cm^2.

19.3 TRIANGLE

For a triangle with base b and corresponding height (altitude) h,
   Area of a triangle = (1/2) x base x height = (1/2) x b x h
The height is the perpendicular from the opposite vertex to the base (or to the base produced).

HERON'S FORMULA. When the three sides a, b and c of a triangle are known but the height is not, we use Heron's formula. First compute the semi-perimeter
   s = (a + b + c) / 2
Then
   Area = sqrt( s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c) )
Worked example: A triangle has sides 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm. s = (13 + 14 + 15)/2 = 42/2 = 21. Area = sqrt(21(21-13)(21-14)(21-15)) = sqrt(21 x 8 x 7 x 6) = sqrt(7056) = 84 cm^2.

EQUILATERAL TRIANGLE. If every side equals a, the area is
   Area = (sqrt(3)/4) x a^2
and the height is (sqrt(3)/2) x a. For example, an equilateral triangle of side 6 cm has area (sqrt(3)/4) x 36 = 9 x sqrt(3) = about 15.59 cm^2.

RIGHT TRIANGLE. In a right-angled triangle the two legs are perpendicular, so one leg is the base and the other is the height: Area = (1/2) x (leg1) x (leg2).

19.4 RHOMBUS

A RHOMBUS is a parallelogram with all four sides equal. Its diagonals bisect each other at right angles. If the diagonals are d1 and d2, then
   Area of a rhombus = (1/2) x d1 x d2
The perimeter is 4a where a is the side; note a = (1/2) sqrt(d1^2 + d2^2) because each half-diagonal forms a right triangle. Worked example: a rhombus with diagonals 16 cm and 12 cm has area (1/2) x 16 x 12 = 96 cm^2; its side is (1/2) sqrt(16^2 + 12^2) = (1/2) sqrt(400) = 10 cm, so its perimeter is 40 cm.

19.5 TRAPEZIUM

A TRAPEZIUM has exactly one pair of parallel sides. If the two parallel sides are a and b and the perpendicular distance (height) between them is h, then
   Area of a trapezium = (1/2) x (a + b) x h
Worked example: parallel sides 10 cm and 6 cm, height 4 cm gives area = (1/2)(10 + 6)(4) = (1/2)(16)(4) = 32 cm^2.

19.6 CIRCLE

For a circle of radius r (diameter d = 2r), using pi = 22/7 or 3.14,
   Circumference (perimeter) = 2 x pi x r = pi x d
   Area = pi x r^2
Worked example: a circle of radius 7 cm has circumference 2 x (22/7) x 7 = 44 cm and area (22/7) x 7 x 7 = 154 cm^2. If the circumference of a circle is 66 cm, then 2 x (22/7) x r = 66, so r = 66 x 7 / (2 x 22) = 10.5 cm.

AREA OF A RING (ANNULUS). A ring is the region between two concentric circles of radii R (outer) and r (inner). Its area is the outer area minus the inner area:
   Area of a ring = pi x R^2 - pi x r^2 = pi (R^2 - r^2) = pi (R + r)(R - r)
Worked example: outer radius 7 cm, inner radius 3.5 cm gives area (22/7)(7^2 - 3.5^2) = (22/7)(49 - 12.25) = (22/7)(36.75) = 115.5 cm^2.

19.7 ARCS, SECTORS AND SEGMENTS

An ARC is a part of the circumference. A SECTOR is the pie-slice region bounded by two radii and the arc between them; the angle between the two radii is the central angle theta (in degrees). Because a full circle is 360 degrees, a sector of angle theta is the fraction theta/360 of the whole circle. Hence
   Length of an arc = (theta/360) x 2 x pi x r
   Area of a sector = (theta/360) x pi x r^2
   Perimeter of a sector = arc length + 2r
Worked example: a sector of a circle of radius 7 cm with central angle 90 degrees. Arc length = (90/360) x 2 x (22/7) x 7 = (1/4) x 44 = 11 cm. Sector area = (90/360) x (22/7) x 49 = (1/4) x 154 = 38.5 cm^2.

A SEGMENT is the region between a chord and its arc. The MINOR segment is cut off by the chord on the smaller side. Its area is found by subtracting the triangle formed by the two radii and the chord from the sector:
   Area of a (minor) segment = area of sector - area of the triangle
                             = (theta/360) x pi x r^2 - (1/2) x r^2 x sin(theta)
For a right-angle (90 degrees) sector of radius 10 cm (pi = 3.14): sector area = (1/4)(3.14)(100) = 78.5 cm^2; triangle area = (1/2)(10)(10) = 50 cm^2; segment area = 78.5 - 50 = 28.5 cm^2.

19.8 COMPOSITE (COMBINED) FIGURES

Many real figures are made by JOINING simple shapes (for example a rectangle with a semicircle on one end, or a triangle sitting on top of a rectangle) or by REMOVING one shape from another (for example a circular hole cut from a square plate). The method is always the same:
   1. Break the figure into standard shapes whose areas you know.
   2. ADD the areas of the parts that are present.
   3. SUBTRACT the areas of the parts that are removed (holes).
Worked example: a rectangle 14 cm by 7 cm has a semicircle of diameter 7 cm attached to one short side. Rectangle area = 14 x 7 = 98 cm^2. Semicircle radius = 3.5 cm, area = (1/2)(22/7)(3.5^2) = (1/2)(22/7)(12.25) = 19.25 cm^2. Total area = 98 + 19.25 = 117.25 cm^2.
Worked example (removal): a square of side 14 cm has a circle of the largest possible size cut out of it. The circle's diameter equals the side, so radius = 7 cm. Remaining area = 14^2 - (22/7)(7^2) = 196 - 154 = 42 cm^2. For the perimeter of a composite figure, add only the OUTER boundary lengths (do not count the internal joins).

SUMMARY

- Perimeter is the length of the boundary (units: cm, m); area is the enclosed surface (units: cm^2, m^2).
- Rectangle: perimeter 2(l + b), area l x b. Square: perimeter 4a, area a^2.
- Parallelogram: area = base x height. Triangle: area = (1/2) x base x height.
- Heron's formula: s = (a + b + c)/2, area = sqrt(s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)).
- Equilateral triangle: area = (sqrt(3)/4) a^2. Rhombus: area = (1/2) d1 d2. Trapezium: area = (1/2)(a + b) h.
- Circle: circumference = 2 pi r, area = pi r^2. Ring: area = pi(R^2 - r^2).
- Arc length = (theta/360) x 2 pi r; sector area = (theta/360) x pi r^2; segment area = sector area - triangle area.
- Composite figures: split into standard shapes, then add present parts and subtract removed parts.

topics.name: Perimeter and Area of Rectangles and Squares
topics.description: Perimeter and area of a rectangle (2(l+b), l x b) and a square (4a, a^2); diagonals; simple applications such as fencing, flooring and tiling.

topics.name: Area of Triangles and Heron's Formula
topics.description: Area of a triangle as (1/2) x base x height; area of an equilateral triangle (sqrt(3)/4)a^2; Heron's formula area = sqrt(s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)) with s = (a+b+c)/2 when all three sides are known.

topics.name: Area of Quadrilaterals (Parallelogram, Rhombus, Trapezium)
topics.description: Area of a parallelogram (base x height), a rhombus ((1/2) d1 d2 using its diagonals) and a trapezium ((1/2)(a+b)h using the two parallel sides and the height).

topics.name: Circumference and Area of a Circle
topics.description: Circumference (2 pi r) and area (pi r^2) of a circle using pi = 22/7 or 3.14; the area of a ring (annulus) between two concentric circles, pi(R^2 - r^2).

topics.name: Arcs, Sectors and Segments
topics.description: Length of an arc ((theta/360) x 2 pi r), area of a sector ((theta/360) x pi r^2) and area of a segment (sector area minus triangle area) for a given central angle theta.

topics.name: Areas of Composite Figures
topics.description: Areas and perimeters of composite figures formed by joining or removing standard shapes; splitting a figure into rectangles, triangles, circles and sectors and adding or subtracting the parts.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: Perimeter and Area of Rectangles and Squares
learning_outcomes.description: Calculate the perimeter and area of rectangles and squares (including diagonals) and solve simple problems on fencing, flooring and tiling.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: Area of Triangles and Heron's Formula
learning_outcomes.description: Find the area of a triangle using (1/2) x base x height, and the area of an equilateral triangle using (sqrt(3)/4) x a^2.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: Area of Triangles and Heron's Formula
learning_outcomes.description: Apply Heron's formula, area = sqrt(s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)) with s = (a+b+c)/2, to find the area of a triangle when its three sides are known.
Compute the area of a parallelogram (base x height), a rhombus ((1/2) d1 d2) and a trapezium ((1/2)(a+b)h).

learning_outcomes.topic_name: Circumference and Area of a Circle
learning_outcomes.description: Calculate the circumference and area of a circle and the area of a ring between two concentric circles using pi = 22/7 or 3.14.
Find the length of an arc, the area of a sector and the area of a segment of a circle for a given central angle.
Determine the area and perimeter of composite figures by splitting them into standard shapes and adding or subtracting the parts.
Analyse and solve multi-step real-life problems on areas of combined figures, including cost, number-of-tiles and shaded-region problems.

chapter_summary.title: Perimeters and Areas of Plane Figures - Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This chapter collects the perimeter and area formulas for the common plane figures - rectangle, square, parallelogram, triangle, rhombus, trapezium and circle - and extends them to arcs, sectors, segments, rings and composite figures. It stresses correct units and worked numerical methods including Heron's formula.

sections.heading: Perimeter and area basics
bullets: Perimeter is the total length of the boundary of a closed figure; it is a length, measured in cm, m or km.
Area is the amount of surface a figure encloses; it is measured in square units such as cm^2 and m^2.
Rectangle: perimeter = 2(l + b), area = l x b, diagonal = sqrt(l^2 + b^2).
Square (side a): perimeter = 4a, area = a^2, diagonal = a x sqrt(2).

sections.heading: Triangles and Heron's formula
bullets: Area of any triangle = (1/2) x base x height, where the height is perpendicular to the base.
Equilateral triangle of side a: area = (sqrt(3)/4) x a^2 and height = (sqrt(3)/2) x a.
When only the three sides a, b, c are known, use Heron's formula with s = (a + b + c)/2.
Heron's formula: area = sqrt(s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c)); e.g. sides 13, 14, 15 give area 84.

sections.heading: Parallelogram, rhombus and trapezium
bullets: Parallelogram: area = base x height, with the height measured perpendicular to the base.
Rhombus: area = (1/2) x d1 x d2, where d1 and d2 are the diagonals (which bisect at right angles).
Trapezium: area = (1/2) x (a + b) x h, where a and b are the parallel sides and h is the distance between them.

sections.heading: Circle and ring
bullets: Circumference of a circle = 2 x pi x r = pi x d; area = pi x r^2 (use pi = 22/7 or 3.14).
A circle of radius 7 cm has circumference 44 cm and area 154 cm^2.
A ring (annulus) between concentric circles of radii R and r has area pi(R^2 - r^2) = pi(R + r)(R - r).

sections.heading: Arcs, sectors, segments and composite figures
bullets: Arc length = (theta/360) x 2 pi r; sector area = (theta/360) x pi r^2; sector perimeter = arc + 2r.
Segment area = sector area - area of the triangle formed by the two radii and the chord.
Composite figures: split into standard shapes, add the parts that are present and subtract the parts removed.
For the perimeter of a composite figure, add only the outer boundary and ignore internal joins.

key_takeaways: Perimeter is a length (cm, m); area is a surface (cm^2, m^2) - always keep the units right.
Rectangle: 2(l+b) and l x b; Square: 4a and a^2; Parallelogram: b x h.
Triangle area = (1/2) b h; equilateral = (sqrt(3)/4) a^2; Heron = sqrt(s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)).
Circle: circumference 2 pi r, area pi r^2; ring = pi(R^2 - r^2).
Arc = (theta/360) 2 pi r; sector = (theta/360) pi r^2; segment = sector - triangle.
Composite figures: split into simple shapes, then add present parts and subtract holes.

glossary.definition: The total length of the boundary of a closed plane figure, measured in units of length such as cm or m.
The measure of the surface enclosed by a plane figure, measured in square units such as cm^2 or m^2.
A quadrilateral with opposite sides equal and all angles right angles; perimeter 2(l+b), area l x b.
A rectangle with all four sides equal (side a); perimeter 4a, area a^2, diagonal a x sqrt(2).
A quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel sides; area = base x height.
A three-sided polygon; area = (1/2) x base x height.
Area = sqrt(s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)) with s = (a+b+c)/2; used when the three sides of a triangle are known.
Half the perimeter of a triangle, s = (a+b+c)/2, used in Heron's formula.
A parallelogram with all four sides equal; area = (1/2) x d1 x d2 using its diagonals.
A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides; area = (1/2)(a+b)h.
The perimeter (boundary length) of a circle, equal to 2 x pi x r.
The region between two concentric circles of radii R and r; area = pi(R^2 - r^2).
The region of a circle bounded by two radii and the arc between them; area = (theta/360) x pi r^2.
A part of the circumference of a circle; length = (theta/360) x 2 pi r for central angle theta.
The region of a circle between a chord and its arc; area = sector area minus the triangle area.

worksheet.title: Worksheet - Perimeters and Areas of Plane Figures
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Use pi = 22/7 unless another value is stated. Show your working and give answers with correct units (cm, m, cm^2, m^2).

questions.question: Find the perimeter and area of a rectangle whose length is 18 cm and breadth is 11 cm.
questions.answer: Perimeter = 2(l + b) = 2(18 + 11) = 2 x 29 = 58 cm. Area = l x b = 18 x 11 = 198 cm^2.
questions.explanation: Apply P = 2(l+b) and A = l x b.

questions.question: The area of a square is 169 cm^2. Find its side and perimeter.
questions.answer: Area = a^2 = 169, so a = sqrt(169) = 13 cm. Perimeter = 4a = 4 x 13 = 52 cm.
questions.explanation: Take the square root to get the side, then P = 4a.

questions.question: Using Heron's formula, find the area of a triangle whose sides are 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm.
questions.explanation: Compute s, then apply Heron's formula.

questions.question: Find the area of an equilateral triangle of side 10 cm. (Take sqrt(3) = 1.73.)
The diagonals of a rhombus are 24 cm and 10 cm. Find its area and perimeter.
questions.explanation: Area from diagonals; side from half-diagonals, then P = 4a.

questions.question: Find the area of a trapezium whose parallel sides are 15 cm and 9 cm and whose height is 8 cm.
A circle has radius 21 cm. Find (a) its circumference and (b) its area. (Take pi = 22/7.)
questions.answer: (a) Circumference = 2 pi r = 2 x (22/7) x 21 = 2 x 22 x 3 = 132 cm. (b) Area = pi r^2 = (22/7) x 21 x 21 = 22 x 3 x 21 = 1386 cm^2.
questions.explanation: Use 2 pi r and pi r^2 with pi = 22/7.

questions.question: A sector of a circle of radius 14 cm has central angle 90 degrees. Find (a) the arc length and (b) the area of the sector. (Take pi = 22/7.)
questions.explanation: Use the sector fraction theta/360 with the circle formulas.

questions.question: A rectangular sheet 20 cm by 14 cm has a semicircle of diameter 14 cm removed from one of its shorter sides. Find the area of the remaining sheet. (Take pi = 22/7.)
questions.answer: Rectangle area = 20 x 14 = 280 cm^2. Semicircle radius = 14/2 = 7 cm; semicircle area = (1/2) pi r^2 = (1/2)(22/7)(49) = (1/2)(154) = 77 cm^2. Remaining area = 280 - 77 = 203 cm^2.
questions.explanation: Composite figure: subtract the removed semicircle from the rectangle.

questions.question: A square lawn of side 28 m has a circular flower bed of the largest possible size in the middle. Find the area of the lawn left outside the flower bed and the cost of grassing it at Rs 5 per m^2. (Take pi = 22/7.)
questions.answer: Square area = 28 x 28 = 784 m^2. Largest circle has diameter 28 m, so radius = 14 m; circle area = (22/7)(14)(14) = 22 x 28 = 616 m^2. Grass area = 784 - 616 = 168 m^2. Cost = 168 x 5 = Rs 840.
questions.explanation: Subtract the inscribed circle from the square, then multiply by the rate.

questions.question: The sides of a triangle are in the ratio 3:4:5 and its perimeter is 36 cm. Find its area.
questions.answer: The sides are 3x, 4x, 5x with 12x = 36, so x = 3; sides are 9, 12, 15 cm. s = 18. Area = sqrt(18 x 9 x 6 x 3) = sqrt(2916) = 54 cm^2.
questions.explanation: Find the sides from the ratio, then Heron.

questions.answer: Circumference = pi d = (22/7)(70) = 220 cm. Distance = 220 x 500 = 110000 cm = 1100 m.
questions.explanation: Distance = circumference x number of turns.

questions.question: A sector has radius 10 cm and central angle 72 degrees. Find its arc length and area. (pi = 3.14.)

A rectangular plot 30 m by 20 m has a 3 m wide gravel path running all around it on the outside. Find the area of the path.
questions.answer: Outer rectangle = (30 + 6) x (20 + 6) = 36 x 26 = 936 m^2. Inner rectangle = 30 x 20 = 600 m^2. Path area = 936 - 600 = 336 m^2.

questions.question: A design is a rectangle 14 cm by 7 cm with a semicircle attached to one of its 7 cm sides. The semicircle has diameter 7 cm. Find the total area. (pi = 22/7.)
A square handkerchief of side 42 cm has 9 equal circular designs (radius 7 cm) printed on it. Find the area left uncovered by the designs. (pi = 22/7.)
questions.answer: Square area = 42 x 42 = 1764 cm^2. One circle = (22/7)(49) = 154 cm^2; nine circles = 9 x 154 = 1386 cm^2. Uncovered area = 1764 - 1386 = 378 cm^2.
questions.explanation: Subtract nine circle areas from the square.

questions.question: A rectangular park 40 m by 30 m has two crossing paths each 2 m wide, one parallel to the length and one parallel to the breadth, through the middle. Find the area of the paths.
questions.answer: Path along length = 40 x 2 = 80 m^2. Path along breadth = 30 x 2 = 60 m^2. They overlap in a 2 x 2 = 4 m^2 square counted twice. Total path area = 80 + 60 - 4 = 136 m^2.
questions.explanation: Add both strips and subtract the overlap once.

A rectangular hall is 20 m long and 15 m wide. It is to be tiled with square tiles of side 50 cm, and a decorative border is to be run along its walls.

(i) Find the area of the hall floor in m^2.
(ii) Find the perimeter of the hall.
(iii) How many 50 cm by 50 cm tiles are needed to cover the floor?
(iv) Find the cost of the border at Rs 30 per metre.
questions.answer:
(i) Area = 20 x 15 = 300 m^2.
(ii) Perimeter = 2(20 + 15) = 2 x 35 = 70 m.
(iii) Each tile is 0.5 m x 0.5 m = 0.25 m^2. Number of tiles = 300 / 0.25 = 1200 tiles.
(iv) Border cost = perimeter x rate = 70 x 30 = Rs 2100.
questions.explanation: Area, perimeter, tile count and border cost for a rectangle.

A triangular road sign has a base of 40 cm and a height of 30 cm. A second warning sign is an equilateral triangle of side 20 cm. (Take sqrt(3) = 1.73.)

(i) Find the area of the first (base-height) sign.
(ii) Write the formula for the area of an equilateral triangle.
(iii) Find the area of the equilateral sign.
(iv) Which sign has the greater area?
questions.answer:
(i) Area = (1/2)(40)(30) = 600 cm^2.
(ii) Area of an equilateral triangle = (sqrt(3)/4) x a^2.
(iii) Area = (1.73/4)(20^2) = (1.73/4)(400) = 1.73 x 100 = 173 cm^2.
(iv) The first sign (600 cm^2) has the greater area than the equilateral sign (173 cm^2).
questions.explanation: Base-height area and equilateral-triangle area compared.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

A goat is tied to a corner of a square shed of side 6 m by a rope of length 7 m in an open field. The goat can graze the region outside the shed that the rope reaches. (Take pi = 22/7.)

(i) The grazable region at the corner is a sector of what angle?
(ii) What is the radius of that sector?
(iii) Find the area the goat can graze.
(iv) If the rope were 3.5 m, what would the grazable area be?
questions.answer:
(i) The two shed walls at the corner make a right angle (90 degrees), so the rope is free to sweep the remaining 360 - 90 = 270 degrees outside the shed. The grazable region is a sector of 270 degrees (a three-quarter circle).
(ii) Radius = length of rope = 7 m.
(iii) Area = (270/360)(22/7)(7^2) = (3/4)(22/7)(49) = (3/4)(154) = 115.5 m^2.
(iv) With rope 3.5 m: area = (270/360)(22/7)(3.5^2) = (3/4)(22/7)(12.25) = (3/4)(38.5) = 28.875 m^2.
questions.explanation: Grazing area as a 270-degree sector at a square corner.

questions.question:

A metal plate is a rectangle 28 cm by 20 cm. Two semicircular pieces of diameter 20 cm are cut off, one from each of the shorter (20 cm) ends. (Take pi = 22/7.)

(i) Find the area of the full rectangle.
(ii) The two semicircles together make what shape, and what is its radius?
(iii) Find the combined area removed.
(iv) Find the area of the remaining plate.
questions.answer:
(i) Rectangle area = 28 x 20 = 560 cm^2.
(ii) The two semicircles of diameter 20 cm together make a full circle of radius 10 cm.
(iii) Circle area removed = (22/7)(10^2) = 2200/7 = about 314.29 cm^2.
(iv) Remaining area = 560 - 314.29 = 245.71 cm^2 (that is 560 - 2200/7 = 1720/7 cm^2).
questions.explanation: Two semicircles form one circle removed from a rectangle.

A rectangular garden is 24 m by 18 m. A path 1.5 m wide is built all around it on the inside, and the rest is planted with grass. Grass seed costs Rs 15 per m^2 and paving costs Rs 40 per m^2.

(i) Find the total area of the garden.
(ii) Find the dimensions and area of the inner grassed rectangle.
(iii) Find the area of the path.
(iv) Find the total cost of grassing and paving.
questions.answer:
(i) Total area = 24 x 18 = 432 m^2.
(ii) Inner rectangle = (24 - 3) x (18 - 3) = 21 x 15 = 315 m^2 (1.5 m removed on each side means 3 m off each dimension).
(iii) Path area = 432 - 315 = 117 m^2.
(iv) Grass cost = 315 x 15 = Rs 4725; paving cost = 117 x 40 = Rs 4680; total = 4725 + 4680 = Rs 9405.
questions.explanation: Inner path and grass areas with combined costs.
